base.text: Every input, and every state it can occupy — including the full directional and motion vocabulary.

base.label: PRESSED — rising edge, true for 1 poll

base.text: PRESSED and RELEASING are true for exactly one poll; UP and HELD persist. A test for 'is it down now' matches PRESSED + HELD. A test for 'was it just pressed' matches PRESSED only. Auto-repeat is a timer on HELD, not a fifth hardware state.
Raw travel, one unsigned byte per trigger. Both triggers are independent — pulling both at once is a legal, ordinary state.

base.label: A trigger has no rising or falling edge of its own — it reports a level, not an event. XInput treats any raw value under XINPUT_GAMEPAD_TRIGGER_THRESHOLD (30) as released; that comparison is what produces a boolean, and the edge model in panel 2 then applies to THAT derived boolean. Choose the threshold deliberately — a lower one fires sooner but chatters near rest.

base.text: each label reads:  compass | numpad | degrees clockwise from N

base.label: All 16 inputs that run this machine:  A / B / X / Y / LB / RB / View / Menu / Guide / Share* / L3 (LS click) / R3 (RS click) / D-Up / D-Down / D-Left / D-Right          (* Share exists on Series X|S controllers only)

Raw axes: LX, LY, RX, RY each report a signed 16-bit value, -32768 to +32767, with +Y up. Radial deadzone constants (XInput): LEFT_THUMB 7849, RIGHT_THUMB 8689 — test the MAGNITUDE, not each axis on its own; per-axis tests carve a square deadzone and cost you the diagonals. The stick is CONTINUOUS: 4-way, 8-way and 16-way are quantisations you impose, normally atan2 binned into equal sectors. Every intermediate angle exists whether or not your code gives it a name. Clicking a stick (L3 / R3) is a separate digital input and runs the panel 2 machine.

base.text: 5. MOTION GESTURES — PATHS THROUGH THE DIRECTIONS
8-WAY TAP — the base alphabet all of these are built from
In every cell up = 8/N and right = 6/E (character facing right). The small digit beside a figure is the numpad direction the motion STARTS from; on DP and RDP the digits 1-2-3 give the order instead.
The 4 machine states of panel 2: UP / PRESSED / HELD / RELEASING. Fully independent — any subset of the four may be down together.
Same 4 machine states. Independent of the trigger sitting behind each one, so LB+LT together is an ordinary state.
Same 4 machine states. Guide is usually intercepted by the console or OS before your code sees it. * Share: Series X|S only.
Same 4 machine states, and fully independent of that stick's X/Y — a stick can be clicked at any deflection, including full tilt.
16 raw switch combinations, but 9 meaningful positions: neutral, 4 cardinals, and 4 diagonals formed by holding two switches at once. Opposing pairs are normally rejected by the hardware.
256 levels each, so 65 536 pairs. No hardware edge of its own: the boolean is derived by comparing against a threshold (XInput uses 30), and the panel 2 machine then runs on that derived value.
A continuous plane, 4 294 967 296 raw (x,y) pairs. Radial deadzone below 7849. Every angle and magnitude between the named directions exists whether or not your code bins it.
Same, with a radial deadzone below 8689. The two sticks are wholly independent, so any left-stick state can be combined with any right-stick state.

base.label: EVERY CONFIGURATION, COUNTED HONESTLY.  Multiply the domains above: 12 freely-combinable digital buttons (2^12) x D-pad (9 legal positions) x triggers (256^2) x sticks (65536^4)  =  44,565,841,414,273,689,896,368,472,064 distinct states, about 4.46 x 10^28. Treating all 16 switches as free instead gives exactly 2^96, about 7.92 x 10^28. Neither number can be drawn, and neither needs to be — the controller reports exactly ONE of them per poll. What a map can show, and what input code is actually written against, is the ALPHABET above: each input's own domain, plus the paths traced through it in panel 5.

ONE POLL RETURNS ONE ROW.   { A B X Y LB RB View Menu Guide Share L3 R3 = 0 or 1 each | D-pad = 4 bits | LT RT = 0 to 255 | LX LY RX RY = -32768 to +32767 }   —   that row is a single point in the space counted in panel 6, and it is the only thing the hardware ever hands you. Everything in panels 2 and 5 is a statement about how that row CHANGES: an edge is the difference between two consecutive rows, and a gesture is a pattern across a window of them. Neither is a thing you can read out of one poll, which is why input code keeps history.

base.text: Shoulder controls sit on the top edge. LT and RT are behind LB and RB and are not visible in this plan view.

findings.symptom: The shell outline is a schematic gamepad silhouette built from hand-chosen vertices rather than traced from a reference. Its grips are longer, its centre notch shallower, and the crotch between the grips lower than on a real Xbox Series/One controller.
findings.consequence: A reader could take the outline as dimensionally representative and infer proportions or control spacing from it. It is accurate only as a topological map: which control sits where relative to the others.

findings.symptom: LB and RB are drawn as straight rounded bars sitting above each shoulder, while the shell's top edge beneath them is a curve. The bars do not follow that curve, and LT and RT sit as separate bars further out again.
findings.consequence: The shoulder controls read as applied labels resting near the controller rather than as moulded hardware on its top edge. A reader could take the gap between bar and shell as a real physical gap.

findings.symptom: In panel 4 the four diagonal rays render as stepped corner-touching quadrants while the four cardinal rays render as solid runs, so the diagonals read slightly lighter than N/S/E/W even in the new orange.
findings.consequence: A reader may perceive a hierarchy in which the cardinal directions are primary and the diagonals secondary. That is false: on an analog stick all eight are equally arbitrary bins of a continuous plane, which the panel's own note says.

findings.symptom: Colour encodes input type consistently in panels 1 to 4, but panel 5's twelve gesture figures stay black even though every one of them is a stick motion and therefore analog. Only the panel 5 header carries the orange.
findings.consequence: A reader scanning by colour could conclude the gestures are a different category from the stick geometry beside them, when they are the same category expressed as paths.

findings.symptom: Panel 5's third row (720, double tap, charge, 8-way) carries much less ink than the first two rows, because two of its four figures are short straight strokes while the rows above are arcs and full circles.
findings.consequence: The row can read as less important, or as unfinished space, rather than as four entries of equal standing.
